newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas -Naphtha edges up, mogas steady.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas -Naphtha edges up, mogas steady.

text.p: Naphtha edged up with overnight crude on Friday while gasoline was steady amid lacklustre demand.

Some traders expected the bearish naphtha market to recover but Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) has awarded its light naphtha export tender for May at a lower level than its March tender -- its last award -- indicating continued weakness.

The 110,000-125,000-barrel cargo for May 2-3 lifting was awarded to Swiss trader Glencore at $1.23 per barrel below Singapore spot quotes, fob Colombo, compared with the 88 cents discount for the March 24-25 cargo.
Saudi Aramco will meet with Asian term lifters in Singapore in the third week of May to negotiate second-half 1997 lifting contracts, traders said.

They said some participants in the first round of bidding, which closed April 4, were however not invited to the meeting as their bids were not competitive. The highest bid for A-180 was heard around $15 per tonne over the Aramco formula.
Gasoline was steady with 92-octane unleaded talked at $23.75/$23.80 per barrel fob Singapore, and 97-octane bid at $24.50 for May lifting.
Fundamentals were still bearish with only a trickle of demand in the region.

Malaysia is seeking 46,000-barrels of 92-octane leaded gasoline in two coastal lots for May delivery while Sri Lanka's CPC issued a tender to buy a combination cargo of 230,000 barrels of gas oil and 40,000 barrels of 95-octane leaded gasoline for May 21-22 delivery to Colombo.
The tender closes on April 29 and offers will be valid until May 1.

But Japanese turnarounds could boost imports, traders said. "Most (Japanese) refineries try to increase their inventories for the summer driving season but many refineries also have turnarounds and have to import reformate," he said.
Japanese refineries' annual maintenance shutdowns started in April and are expected to last until October. But most are concentrated in May and June, traders said.
They said Japan's monthly imports of four to five 100,000-barrel cargoes of reformate could be raised to as many as eight cargoes in May and June.
"There are several requirements from Japanese refiners. After Golden Week, they will decide their position," a trader said. The Golden Week holidays in Japan last from end April to early May.
In anticipation of increased reformate demand in Japan, South Korean refiner Yukong Ltd is considering the restart of its 8,000-bpd reforming unit in May, a source said.
Weak gasoline and petrochemical prices forced Yukong, the country's largest refiner to shut the unit on January 24 with plans to restart at the end of June.
"Yukong is considering starting its reformer in May ... especially with Japanese demand for reformate expected to increase in the second quarter," a source said.
